passage:
The town library began lending e-books. Readers could borrow books without visiting the building.
This helped people who lived far away or could not leave home easily. But some older readers missed talking to librarians and walking between shelves.
The library kept both services. It also started teaching people how to use e-books on their phones and tablets.
The head librarian said a library should not become only digital or only physical. It should meet readers in different ways.
The online library expanded access. The building still offered quiet, help, and community.
A book can travel through a screen, but a library is also a place.
